preamble: Rhotacism of the alveolar nasal: intervocalic /n/ loses its nasality and becomes the alveolar tap [ɾ]. The best-known cases are in the Balkans: Tosk Albanian (against Gheg, which keeps n) and Istro-Romanian and some northern Romanian dialects, where intervocalic n in Latin-derived words became r.

examples.note: Intervocalic n became the tap r [ɾ] in Tosk; Gheg keeps n.
Same change; also Shqypnia vs Tosk Shqipëria 'Albania', druni vs druri 'the wood'.
Christian Latin loanwords also show the change, which dates the Gheg–Tosk split to after the 4th century AD.
Istro-Romanian and some northern Romanian dialects turned intervocalic [n] into [ɾ] in words of Latin origin.
